intended_object: The canonical bijection between the dependent sum Σ' i, β i (PSigma) and Σ i, β i (Sigma) for a type family β : α → Type. Both encode the disjoint union of the family, and the map sends ⟨i, b⟩ to ⟨i, b⟩. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The forward and inverse maps both repackage ⟨a.1, a.2⟩. The two composites are definitionally the identity, so this is the identity bijection between two encodings of the same disjoint union. The binder {α} has no type annotation, so its type is inferred from Sigma, which requires α : Type _ and β : α → Type _. That is the most general setting in which both sides typecheck: a PSigma over arbitrary Sorts cannot be equivalent to a Sigma type. So the generality is maximal. One could argue this is a Lean-specific bridge between the PSigma and Sigma encodings with no counterpart in the literature. Read as a bijection between types, though, it is correct and fully general.
